---
title: "Publish a Quarto Website"
---

## What Quarto does

Quarto combines Markdown, executable code, citations, and outputs into a
website or report. A publishable data project should render from a fresh R
session without relying on objects left in the Console.

Current RStudio releases include Quarto. To verify the command-line tool, run
this in the **Terminal**, not the R Console:

```bash
quarto check
```

The R package named `quarto` is optional; it is not required to render a Quarto
project from RStudio or the Terminal.

## Create a website project

In RStudio, choose **File → New Project → New Directory → Quarto Website**. A
basic project contains:

- `_quarto.yml` — site-wide configuration;
- `index.qmd` — the home page;
- other `.qmd` pages;
- optional `styles.css`; and
- an `.Rproj` file.

Use folders such as:

```text
project/
├── _quarto.yml
├── index.qmd
├── methods.qmd
├── analysis.qmd
├── data/
│   ├── raw/
│   └── processed/
├── scripts/
├── images/
└── outputs/
```

## Configure navigation correctly

For a Quarto website, navigation belongs under `website: navbar:`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "My Data Story"
  navbar:
    left:
      - text: Home
        href: index.qmd
      - text: Methods
        href: methods.qmd
      - text: Analysis
        href: analysis.qmd

format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    toc: true
```

Use `.qmd` targets in the configuration. Quarto creates the corresponding HTML
files during rendering.

## Make every page reproducible

Each page should load the packages and data it needs. Do not assume another page
runs first.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(tidyverse)

analysis_data <- readRDS("data/processed/analysis_data.rds")
```

Test with:

1. **Session → Restart R**;
2. delete any temporary objects from the Environment;
3. run `quarto render` from the project root; and
4. inspect the rendered site and Terminal output.

## Preview and publish

Preview locally with the RStudio Render button or:

```bash
quarto preview
```

To publish to Quarto Pub, create an account at
[quartopub.com](https://quartopub.com/) and run:

```bash
quarto publish
```

Follow the prompts to choose Quarto Pub and authorize the account. Republishing
updates the existing site when you select the same destination.

Publishing is not a substitute for archiving. Preserve the source data, code,
and a dated methods note in a repository or institutional storage location.

## Include files readers need

Quarto automatically includes figures generated by a page, but downloadable
data or standalone assets may need to be declared:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  resources:
    - data/processed/*.csv
    - downloads/*
```

Do not publish sensitive data, credentials, embargoed material, or files you do
not have permission to redistribute.

## Accessibility and verification

Before publishing:

- add informative alt text to images;
- use descriptive link text instead of “click here”;
- ensure color is not the only way a chart communicates meaning;
- test the site on a phone-sized window;
- check that navigation and download links work;
- verify titles, captions, sources, units, and dates; and
- render once from a clean session.

## Removing a published site

Deleting the local folder does not remove a published copy. Use the provider's
site dashboard to delete it. Confirm the exact target before deletion; a
published URL may already be cited or shared.
